title: Opener: Five or six?
materials: The badge sheet, for its “five branches” line

displayContent.headline: How many branches?
displayContent.body: Your patrol has 60 seconds. Write every branch of the U.S. Armed Forces you can name.

leaderScript: Give each patrol 60 seconds to write every branch of the Armed Forces on the whiteboard.
Read the badge sheet’s line about “five branches,” then ask who’s right.
Press R to reveal all six. Treat it as a puzzle, not a correction: the sheet is dated 2018, and the Space Force came in December 2019.
Ask the two discussion questions, then move on.

discussionQuestions.question: Which branch is the oldest?
discussionQuestions.answer: The Army, from the Continental Army of June 14, 1775. The Navy and Marines followed later that year.

discussionQuestions.question: Which branch isn’t in the Department of Defense?
discussionQuestions.answer: The Coast Guard. In peacetime it’s under the Department of Homeland Security.

ifShortOnTime: Skip the whiteboard race. Ask “five or six?” out loud and reveal.
lowVolunteerNote: Runs fine with one leader as a whole-group activity.
